evals.name: happy-three-way
evals.prompt: After the deploy I did to myapp-staging, I want to confirm ConfigHub, Argo, and the cluster all agree on the checkout unit.
evals.expected_output: Builds the four-column table (image, revision, health, owner) using cub function do get-container-image + cub unit get for the ConfigHub column, argocd app get for the controller column, kubectl get + annotations for the cluster column. Reports agreement explicitly across all four rows. Offers --web review links. Hands off to release-verify as the next step. Does not mutate.

evals.name: cluster-mutated-out-of-band
evals.prompt: I'm suspicious someone poked the checkout deployment directly via kubectl. Can you prove whether that happened?
evals.expected_output: Populates the three-way table, identifies that the cluster image disagrees with ConfigHub+controller (or that ownerReferences/annotations indicate out-of-band change), names the divergence explicitly as 'cluster ≠ ConfigHub, controller agrees with ConfigHub — drift on the cluster side', and recommends a drift-handling path (cub unit refresh + reconcile) as the next step without running it.

evals.name: controller-not-authenticated
evals.prompt: Run a three-way check on the payments unit in myapp-prod.
evals.expected_output: Attempts the argocd (or flux) CLI for the controller column, detects it isn't authenticated or reachable, reports that column as 'unknown — argocd CLI not authenticated' rather than faking agreement, completes the ConfigHub and cluster columns, and produces a partial table with the caveat surfaced to the user. Does not assume agreement where data is missing.
